{"self_assessment": "Impact
I built the lower tail lobe of our fish. I picked up where Maya's bottom line ended and carried it out to the tail tip by tracing stroke 2 from the end of the existing line. The tail is what makes the outline read as a fish, so this was a key piece. I also inspected the tail region several times, including after the lobe was laid and again before the push, and reported that both lobes were connected out to the tips. At the push, my by-eye trace showed about 107 of 108 standing dominoes connected to the start.

Execution
I took on the lower lobe, laid it in two short batches, and checked the joins afterward. I looked closely at the tail area at several points rather than assuming it was fine. Once the run was connected, I kept my hands off it so I wouldn't risk a bump or break what was already standing.

Collaboration
I kept clear of the nose while Priya and Maya worked close together there, which reduced the chance of bumps. I agreed the handoffs out loud: Leo on the upper lobe, me on the lower lobe, and Maya stopping short of the fork. I also flagged the unconnected pale dominoes in the top line so the people nearest could fix them. I kept the table updated on the tail's status.

Leadership
I helped set the division of labor at the tail by proposing who would take which lobe. I asked Maya directly whether she wanted to finish the lower lobe or hand it off, so there was no overlap or gap. In the last minutes I reinforced the hands-off discipline so the run stayed intact for the push.", "my_share_percent": 22}
